findings.finding: The proposed config mutation (flipping refs/changes/* to a forced `+refs/changes/*:refs/changes/*`) does not mechanically address the named root cause (a change ref that had not yet replicated / was missing on the mirror at validation time). A force refspec only alters rejection behavior for non-fast-forward updates; an absent/lagging ref is a fast-forward-from-nothing that the existing non-force refspec already permits, so force does not make the ref appear sooner. The refspec already exists (config line 63; ADR-0021; the plan's own RED premise), so the real fix for lag is the replication trigger — which needs no `+`.

Gerrit replication config.md (gerrit.googlesource.com/wikimedia mirror): leading '+' causes 'git push --force'; refs/changes/NN patchset refs are immutable per-patchset so missing refs are created by ordinary non-force push
findings.finding: The plan switches the change-ref replication refspec from the existing non-force 'refs/changes/*:refs/changes/*' to the FORCE variant '+refs/changes/*:refs/changes/*' without justifying force over the established non-force approach that ADR-0021 and the current replication.config deliberately chose. The documented rationale (replication.config lines 14-16; ADR-0021 §3/Consequences) is that non-force (no leading '+') is the 'core safety property' rejecting non-fast-forward clobbers, and that replication lag/misses are already tolerated by the checkout-gerrit-change-action gerrit-url fallback. The RCA describes a MISSING immutable patchset ref, which an ordinary non-force push during a full replication sweep would publish — so the prior-art (non-force + trigger replication) plausibly solves the failure without force.
findings.location: Plan section 'Plan' bullet 1 / AC 'The versioned Gerrit replication config publishes +refs/changes/*:refs/changes/*'
scenarios: A previously-replicated change ref exists on GitHub with different content; force push silently rewrites it on the mirror, weakening the one-way-door / append-only guarantee ADR-0010/0021 rely on
The actual missing-ref failure would already be fixed by a non-force full replication sweep, making the force change an unjustified departure from prior art

findings.finding: The plan flips the durable refs/changes/* replication refspec from non-force to force (+refs/changes/*:refs/changes/*) without addressing the documented safety trade-off: the existing replication.config calls the non-force refspec 'the core safety property' (a non-fast-forward push is REJECTED rather than clobbering GitHub), and monitoring_s5.tf's replication_errors alarm watches REJECTED_NONFASTFORWARD precisely to detect ADR-0010 one-way-door / history-divergence violations.
